newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Diplomat says Malaysian students safe in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Diplomat says Malaysian students safe in Australia.

text.p: The Australian High Commissioner to Malaysia said on Thursday his country is a safe place to study despite racial taunts suffered by some Malaysian students recently.
Speaking on a live talk show on a private Malaysian television channel, Bill Farmer said racial incidents reported in the Malaysian press were the work of "a small fringe group".
"Australia by any standard remains safe, welcoming, and I'd say for students, a quiet place and a fun place to live," Farmer said on the Face to Face programme broadcast by the TV3 station.
Malaysia's 11,000 students in Australia have come under the spotlight this week following a report that several have been the victims of racial abuse.
Malaysian student leader Adrina Shazlin Shukor was verbally abused by Australian youths for being Asian, the national Bernama news agency reported at the weekend.
On Monday, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said Malaysia might consider calling home its students in Australia if reported threats against them were found to be serious.
Farmer said the majority of Australians are against racial discrimination. He described the racial slurs hurled at Adrina as "totally unacceptable behaviour".
"It's clearly the product of a small fringe group of people. I'm not proud as an Australian to have such people as part of my country," Farmer said.
Adrina, who appeared on the same show, said she cried after the verbal assault outside a convenience store by a group of "well-attired" Australian youths.
"They were saying all these very impolite words to me...I just stood there frozen, crying," she said.
Racism has become a major issue in Australia since independent politician Pauline Hanson said in her maiden Parliament speech in September that Australia was being swamped by Asians.
Hanson called for an immediate moratorium on immigration, but Australian leaders have distanced themselves from Hanson's comments and said she does not reflect the official view.
